question: Can the existing neural input space learn boxing maintenance directly when rewarded for extending an established combo, independently of ring-out ability?
diagnosis: In the m2110 development clock at 0ms from the same K3 B state, both W-tap and the frozen sumo hybrid dealt a sprint hit at 11181.312ms. W-tap had 2.130 blocks of horizontal separation and prevented the simultaneous return. The hybrid had 1.961 blocks and took an accepted return in that same drain. W-tap completed three further cycles versus one. In another matched m2093 state both dealt the same first impulse; the hybrid advanced closer and lost two cycles. More forward pressure can shorten the spacing margin despite equal outbound knockback.
plant: Original 16 training tapes. Four declared timing offsets per donor (0/0, 13/31, 37/7, 23/43 ms for A/B); both seats, both symmetric RTTs, full reach, 20 CPS, 2000ms defender click delay, 20s native limit. Timing variants count as correlated development draws. Use the first K3 common W-tap state per opening, never separate entry cohorts.
method: Compare directly optimized affine and recurrent networks with an MLP. Warm-start from sumo weights and random initialization. Rerun the exact W-tap observation and actually applied key history into each candidate, retaining committed queues. Optimize paired improvement in qualified further fresh hits, equally weighting donor scenarios. Stop suffixes at accepted return, inactivity over 1000 ms or the common horizon. Use the same stop for W-tap. Score plain return-only and missed fresh windows separately at evaluation.
promotion: Select one frozen specialist on the eight already exposed development selection clocks. Evaluate K3, K5 and K10 on a subsequent set of new timing donors after freeze. Native comparison against W-tap using common W-tap acquisition and client-cue handoff. Report enrollment, timing bins, exposure, failures and censoring, not just round margin. No human claim.
